title: Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC): One Award per Surviving Spouse
content:
## Rule

A surviving spouse holds at most one Dependency and Indemnity Compensation (DIC) award — a limit of 1 award per surviving spouse — and that award is based on one veteran's death.

An award is established only when the spouse holds no DIC award whose status is authorized, running or suspended.

Parents' DIC and DIC paid to children in their own right are separate benefits and are never paid on the spouse's award.

## What the rule looks at

- **Whose awards.** The awards held by the same surviving spouse — the person for whom the new award would be established.
- **Which record decides.** The spouse's DIC awards as they stand in VA's records before the new award is established, read by their status. What the caller says about earlier awards does not replace the recorded status.
- **Which statuses stand in the way.** Authorized (granted, first payment not yet released), running (being paid) and suspended (payments withheld). An award whose status is terminated is not among them.

## Status table

| The spouse's existing DIC award has status | Does it stand in the way of establishing an award under this rule? |
|---|---|
| Authorized | Yes |
| Running | Yes |
| Suspended | Yes |
| Terminated | No |
| The spouse holds no DIC award | No |

A "No" in this table means only that this rule does not stand in the way; it is not by itself a grant of an award.

## Separate benefits

| Benefit | Paid on the surviving spouse's DIC award? |
|---|---|
| Parents' DIC | Never — a separate benefit |
| DIC paid to a child in the child's own right | Never — a separate benefit |

## Hypothetical cases

1. A surviving spouse's only DIC award shows the status suspended because payments were withheld. Under this rule, no second award is established for that spouse while that award stands as suspended.
2. A surviving spouse's earlier DIC award shows the status terminated. That terminated award does not, under this rule, stand in the way of establishing an award.
3. A veteran's parent receives parents' DIC. That benefit is not paid on the surviving spouse's award and does not count as the spouse holding a DIC award.
